samples.summary: Table-cell Backspace bypasses Doc.deleteBackward entirely, so the delta's new "Enter matches Backspace" list exit does not hold inside table cells
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1896-1925 — `handleBackspace` takes a cell-specific branch (`if (bsCellInfo) { ... }`) that only does `docDeleteText` / `mergeBlocks` / no-op (line 1920) and never calls `this.doc.deleteBackward`. By contrast `handleEnter`'s cell branch (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2049) does call `docSplitBlock` → `Doc.splitBlock`, which this delta changed to restore the remembered heading. Net effect inside a table cell: Enter on an empty bulleted Heading 2 now leaves a Heading 2, while Backspace on the same block still does nothing (first block in cell) or merges — the opposite of what the new comment at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:265-266 and docs/design/docs/docs.md:166-170 assert. Related bypasses of the same branch: `handleWordBackspace` (text-editor.ts:2003) and `handleLineBackspace` (text-editor.ts:2805) both `return` when the block index is 0, so Ctrl/Alt+Backspace on the first empty bulleted block never reaches the exit either. Fix belongs in the view-layer cell/word/line backspace paths (or the design doc must scope the claim to the body path).

samples.summary: Caller comment still documents the pre-delta contract of splitBlock's in-place list exit
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2084-2086: `if (newBlockId === pos.blockId) { // Block was converted in-place (e.g., empty list → paragraph)` — after this delta, `Doc.splitBlock` converts the empty list-item to the remembered heading, not necessarily a paragraph, so this consumer comment describes the old behaviour.

samples.summary: unlistedBlockType keys purely on `headingLevel !== undefined`, and the delta now applies it on every Enter/Backspace, so any list-item carrying a headingLevel from a non-toggle source would silently become a heading
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:340 returns `{type:'heading'}` for any block with `headingLevel` set, regardless of how it got there; document.ts:267 and :304 now feed every empty-list-item keystroke through it. I checked the plausible producers and none currently emit list-item+headingLevel: packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:128-141 (`resolveBlockMeta` sets headingLevel only for h1–h6, list-item only for li), packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:136-146 (headingLevel always paired with blockType 'heading'), packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:256-257 (`applySplitBlock` deletes headingLevel when the new type is not heading), packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2043-2051/2136-2141 (Yorkie split does not copy headingLevel onto a list-item). So this is a latent-coupling risk rather than a confirmed break; confirming would need an audit of any future/external writer (e.g. backend docs-tree round trip at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:260, which preserves headingLevel on any block type).
searchedFor: grep headingLevel in packages/docs/src, packages/backend, packages/cli/src

finding.summary: Two other "exit the list" paths still hardcode 'paragraph', bypassing `unlistedBlockType`
finding.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:298-300 (`if (block.type === 'list-item' && blockText.length === 0) this.setBlockType(blockId, 'paragraph')`) and `Doc.deleteBackward` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:263-265 both leave a list by forcing `'paragraph'`. These are the Enter-on-empty-bullet and Backspace-on-empty-bullet exits, the most common way a user leaves a list. After this change, exiting a bulleted Heading 2 via the toolbar restores the heading while exiting via Enter/Backspace silently destroys the remembered level (and `setBlockType('paragraph')` deletes `headingLevel` outright, so it is unrecoverable). The `unlistedBlockType` doc comment claims it keeps the exit behaviour from drifting across implementations, but these two model-layer exits were not routed through it. Fix belongs at document.ts:264 and :299 (call `unlistedBlockType(curBlock/block)`), not in the diff.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that Doc.deleteBackward (document.ts:263-265) and Doc.splitBlock (document.ts:298-300) still hardcode setBlockType(..., 'paragraph') when leaving an empty list item, bypassing unlistedBlockType. Reading the file, both sites already route through the helper: deleteBackward at document.ts:263-269 does `const exit = unlistedBlockType(curBlock); this.setBlockType(pos.blockId, exit.type, exit.opts);` and splitBlock at document.ts:301-307 does `const exit = unlistedBlockType(block); this.setBlockType(blockId, exit.type, exit.opts);`. unlistedBlockType is imported at document.ts:28 and defined at types.ts:337-344, restoring {type:'heading', opts:{headingLevel}} when headingLevel is present. A grep for 'list-item' across document.ts shows only these two exit paths plus the non-exit `newType` default (document.ts:329) and the horizontal-rule/page-break branch (document.ts:313), neither of which is a list exit. The quoted bypassing code is not present, so the alleged Enter/Backspace divergence from the toolbar exit does not exist.
